entry.title: Attachment Virus/Malicious Content Scanning Capability in SAP SuccessFactors
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We're reviewing the attachment security capabilities of SAP SuccessFactors as part of our organization's cybersecurity assessment, and we'd appreciate some clarification on how the platform handles files uploaded by users.

Could anyone help confirm the following?

  1. Does SAP SuccessFactors perform virus or malware scanning on uploaded attachments?
  2. If yes, is the scanning performed natively within SuccessFactors or through an integrated third-party antivirus/security service?
  3. Which SuccessFactors modules or attachment areas are covered by this scanning mechanism?
  4. What types of malicious or potentially harmful content can be detected?
  5. If a malicious file is detected, is it automatically blocked, quarantined, or rejected?
  6. Are there any file size, file type, or format limitations related to the scanning process?
  7. Are any logs, alerts, or audit records available when a malicious attachment is detected?
  8. Is there any customer configuration available to enable, disable, or customize attachment security/scanning?
  9. Does SAP recommend any additional security controls or third-party integrations for attachment virus/malware protection?

    We're specifically looking for SAP standard capabilities and any relevant documentation or SAP Notes that describe the recommended approach.

    Thanks in advance for your guidance!

entry.title: Any workaround for configuring overtime on non-working days AND holidays falling on a working day to
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We need to configure attendance quota so employees can record overtime in two scenarios:

  1. On weekends (non-working days)
  2. On a public holiday that happens to fall on what would normally be a working day

    Based on what we've found, this combination currently can't be configured together in standard Time Tracking, and SAP has logged it as a known issue with product engineering investigating, with no workaround documented yet.

    Since our go-live can't wait on a fix timeline, I wanted to check with the community:

    1. Has anyone found a practical interim workaround even a partial one for either of these two OT scenarios individually, if not both together?
    2. Is anyone handling this through a custom time valuation rule instead of relying on standard attendance quota configuration?
    3. Has SAP given any indication of a target release for a fix, beyond "under investigation"?
    4. For those who hit this: did you end up processing holiday-that-falls-on-a-working-day overtime through payroll adjustments outside the system instead?

Thanks in advance for any real-world experience here!

entry.title: Carryover and Forfeiture Rules with Mid-Year Work Schedule Changes
entry.content:
Business Context:
Our carryover rules allow employees to carry a max of 5 unused days into the new leave year, with anything above that forfeited on the carryover date. Employees who change work schedule (e.g., full-time to part-time) mid-year have their annual entitlement prorated, but carryover calculation seems to use the current FTE at time of carryover, not a prorated blend across the year.

Questions for the community:

  1. Have you dealt with prorating carryover/forfeiture itself (not just entitlement) when FTE changes mid-year?
  2. Does the standard carryover rule scenario support referencing historical FTE/work schedule snapshots, or does it only read current values?
  3. Any workaround using Time Account “rule-based” carryover vs. a scheduled job (Integration Center/CPI) that recalculates carryover manually?
  4. How do you communicate/document forfeiture amounts to employees to avoid disputes (e.g., an automated notification at carryover time)?

entry.title: How Are You Configuring Remote Workers in Employee Central?
entry.content:
Hello SuccessFactors Community,

We’re reviewing how to represent fully remote employees in Employee Central and would appreciate hearing what other organizations are doing.

The standard Location foundation object represents a company’s physical work locations. It doesn’t, by itself, represent a remote employee’s actual work address when that address differs from their assigned office.

Our current approach is to use Work Address Override (WAO) to capture the address where a remote employee performs their work, alongside a work classification field identifying the employee as remote, onsite, or hybrid.

We see some operational considerations with this approach. Downstream integrations and processes need to read from the correct address source for payroll, tax, compliance forms, and reporting. Address changes when an employee moves also need careful handling to keep related records and processes aligned.

What approach does your organization use for remote-worker configuration in Employee Central? Are you satisfied with how it supports ongoing monitoring, address changes, and downstream integrations? What would you recommend or do differently?

Thanks for sharing your experience.
